blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422), with automated regression coverage added (r424). Separate, not-yet-fixed discovery from r424: HEAD has never been buildable from a byte-for-byte fresh clone (native_vulkan_backend.cpp has never had Vulkan linkage in any committed CMakeLists.txt) -- named for a dedicated future cycle. r425/r426 made real, now byte-level-confirmed progress on the next open PRODUCT question (presented_frames=0/present=0, r418): VdSwap (the real Xbox 360 kernel present call) IS called by the guest, and its validation path does sometimes drain genuinely new ring content containing real PM4 packets (type-3 headers decoding to known opcodes like 0x36/0x46/0x3c) -- but r426 dumped the actual guest memory around the cursor VdSwap passes (correcting a methodology slip along the way: ctx.r3 for this function lives at ctx+0x00, not the +0x08 offset that works elsewhere -- same class of pitfall as r412, caught before publishing) and found ZERO occurrences of the XE_SWAP opcode (0x64) or its SWAP fourcc signature across all 5 captured calls. A 75s probe window (3x the original 25s) was also tried and changes nothing -- the ring's activity plateaus at the same point either way, ruling out 'just needs more time to reach its first swap.' This closes the r292-r296 'ring discovery might be buggy' hypothesis at the byte level: the guest genuinely never constructs an XE_SWAP packet in the observed window, despite calling VdSwap repeatedly and despite rendering real geometry (up to 50 draws in one batch). Named for r427: read sub_821F03B0 (VdSwap's direct caller) line by line, and its callers (sub_8234F558/sub_8233E0A8/sub_8233B5A0) if needed, to find either the condition gating XE_SWAP emission or what's actually blocking the guest from progressing toward its first real swap at all -- likely a different subsystem (rendering/scene-state) than the allocator/threading chain r399-r422 already closed. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r426 were committed individually.
